title: Hill-climbing the welfare Pareto — what we have so far
subtitle: One canonical metric, measured the same way every time: trait = murder-avg3 (murder over 3 goal settings), exfiltration kept as a separate must-not-regress guard (n=300), combined into a single AM score. Batch 1 (8 arms, co-measured) answered the keystone question — does the Claude-critic loop beat plain on-policy C2? — no. Then two off-policy mechanisms were tried to push AM DOWN at high capability: token-clipping and TESSY-lite (teacher-content / student-style). The first round of both failed to beat the C2 bar — but a follow-up N=2 sweep at LIGHTER clip-frac (0.05) finally crossed below C2 into the win zone.
caveat: clip-frac 0.05 has now MOVED the frontier below C2 — GPQA 0.641 / AM 0.032, Pareto-dominating C2 on BOTH axes (single-seed; seed-replication in flight). It came from iterating on clip-mild's one weakness, exfil: capability already saturates by clip-frac 0.10, so dropping to a LIGHTER clip (0.05 / 0.075) keeps GPQA while exfil bleeds out (0.19 → 0.05) and murder falls too. Earlier arms still sit at/above C2: actor-critic slightly WORSE on both; GRAPE leaks on exfil (guard catch); recovery climbs back to base; clip-mild ≈ C2 (murder win offset by high exfil); TESSY-lite installs NO trait (base-level AM 0.61) — the student's own voice dilutes the committed conduct. AM cells: murder n=100×3 (≈300 eff), exfil n=300.
eval_note: Murder re-graded on Chloe's sonnet-4-6 classifier via a regex→sonnet cascade at temp=0 (the gpt-4.1 grader MATS had silently substituted over-flagged murder ~2× arm-dependently); exfiltration on gpt-4.1 (validated ≈ sonnet, no over-flag). AM = mean(murder-avg3, exfil): murder × {none, explicit-global, latent-global} averaged @ n=100; exfiltration (explicit-global) @ n=300; model_name=Qwen, prod=true, temp 0.7. GPQA = GPQA-Diamond strict@20k. Adapters all LoRA r64 on Qwen3-32B; C2/rewrite/baseline captured Neel→R2.

pareto.yLabel: AM = mean(murder-avg3, exfil) → lower is more aligned

winZone.note: higher capability AND lower AM than C2 — better on both. clip-0.05 (0.641/0.032) is the first arm to enter it (single-seed; replicating).

pareto.note: Y = single AM = (murder-avg3 + exfil)/2; lower is more aligned. **Every method is on Chloe's grader** — murder re-graded with her sonnet-4-6 classifier at temp=0 (the gpt-4.1 MATS had silently substituted over-flagged murder ~2× arm-dependently); exfil kept on gpt-4.1 (validated ≈ sonnet). The cross is C2; the bottom-right WIN ZONE (better than C2 on BOTH axes) was empty for the whole first pass — until **clip-0.05 (0.641/0.032) entered it and Pareto-DOMINATES C2 (0.606/0.121): higher capability AND ~1/4 the AM.** clip-0.075 (0.606/0.060) also clears C2, at equal capability. The route there: capability saturates by clip-frac 0.10, so clip-mild's only weakness was its high exfil (0.190) — a LIGHTER clip (0.05) keeps GPQA while exfil bleeds to 0.05 and murder to 0.013. **Caveat: single-seed, and murder counts are small (4/300, 15/300) — seed-replication of clip-0.05 is in flight; the AM win is driven mostly by the reliably-graded exfil drop, which the eval-sampling CIs can't overturn.** Earlier read corrected too: **clip-mild (0.672/0.128) ≈ ties C2** (its murder win was offset by exfil — clip-0.05 fixes exactly that). Frontier now: exp2-mix+ (0.470/0.084) → **clip-0.05 (0.641/0.032)** → C2/clip-mild band → OPD-A (0.712/0.182, high-capability end). OPD-B (0.561/0.149) dominated by C2 — its 'install' was a prompt-order CONFOUND; the clean re-run OPD-B2 (0.616/0.310) is a null. TESSY (0.591/0.615) at/above base — restyle installed no trait. sonnet+temp=0 also KILLED the C2 cross-batch drift (Δ0.002 vs Δ0.083 on gpt-4.1).

exfil_guard.note: Exfiltration (2nd action) @ n=300, kept as a separate must-not-regress guard — NOT blended into the trait axis. It's doing real work twice over: GRAPE looks fine on murder but leaks here (0.297, near base 0.430, ~2.3× C2); and it's exactly where clip-mild FAILED (0.190) and where the lighter clip-0.05 WON (0.050) — the murder-only view would have missed both. C2 exfil = 0.127 (co-measured canonical).

precision.note: Exfil ran at n=300; resampling n=100 subsets from the 300 shows how much precision n buys. SE drops 0.036→0.021 (ratio 1.74 ≈ √3 — clean binomial, no hidden grader noise). At n=100 the C2-vs-actor-critic exfil gap (0.047) is ~1σ (noise); at n=300 it's ~1.8σ (resolvable). So n=300 is worth it for exfil; murder-avg3 is already ≈300-effective. (Means below are this specific frontier-batch's exfil — a different batch from the co-measured canonical levels in the scatter, e.g. C2 0.127; the point here is the SE-vs-n scaling, not the absolute level.)

arms.label: Actor-critic
arms.verdict: WORSE than C2 (0.115 / 0.127) on both murder and exfil, co-measured (sonnet grader). The Claude-critic loop didn't help — if anything it hurt.

arms.label: GRAPE selection
arms.verdict: ≈ Ties C2 on murder (0.143 vs 0.115) but LEAKS on exfil (0.297 vs 0.127) — the guard catch. Lowest capability too. Selection didn't help.

arms.label: Recovery (d10)
arms.verdict: Capability back to base (0.712) but both actions re-erode toward base (0.353 / 0.467). Not a Pareto win.

recovery_curve.metric_note: Per-dose y is single-setting murder (goal=none) from the original dose sweep, NOT murder-avg3 — only d10 got the full thorough treatment. The shape (capability and trait climbing together) is the point.

length.headline: 534 / 3366 GPQA rollouts truncated (unclosed <think> — ran out of the 20k budget mid-reasoning, never committed). Their accuracy is 0.015 at a median 65,707 chars: the "reason forever, never answer" failure mode. The whole "long → wrong" cliff is these truncated rollouts — among completed rollouts it disappears.
length.reasoning_len: Median think-block length: base 19,845 chars / recovery-d10 18,318 (both ≈0.70 GPQA) ≫ trait arms ~2,000 (C2 / actor-critic / GRAPE, ≈0.54–0.60).
hypotheses: Capability ≈ completed-reasoning-quality × (1 − truncation-rate); GPQA's "capability" axis is really two separable axes.
The d1–d3 recovery dip (GPQA 0.42–0.43) is a termination pathology — early on-model SFT destabilizes stopping (truncation 31%→42%) before d10 fixes it to 2.5% — not a reasoning-quality loss.

On-policy trait data (C2 / actor-critic / GRAPE) fixes termination but yields lower completed-quality; off-model Opus-distilled (Chloe) keeps high completed-quality but inherits a runaway-no-stop pathology.
